name: NIQ Global Intelligence plc

sentences: NIQ Global Intelligence plc files with the SEC under "Services-Computer Programming, Data Processing, Etc.", based in IL, and has been publicly reporting for 0 years.
It reported $4.1bn of revenue over the trailing four quarters, up 11.1% against the same quarter a year earlier.
Listed on NYSE, it is still consuming cash, with roughly 20 months of runway at the current burn.
summary.note: Assembled from filing metadata and XBRL figures. Not editorial judgement - and rule 7 asks whether *you* can explain it, so rewrite this in your own words before you rely on it.

bull.text: Revenue grew 11.1% year on year (Q1 2026 vs Q1 2025), reaching $1.1bn in the quarter.

bear.text: The company is loss-making at the operating line (-1.0% margin). Profitability is a forecast, not a fact.
The operating loss widened by $25.9m against the same quarter a year earlier - it is getting worse, not better.
About 20 months of cash at the current burn ($362.3m against $217.2m a year). A company that must raise is a company that raises on the buyer's terms.
Diluted share count rose 20.4% over the year (Q1 2026 vs Q1 2025). The company can grow while your share of it shrinks, and this is the number most commentary ignores.
Debt of $3.6bn against equity of $915.9m. Leverage decides who controls the outcome if trading deteriorates, and it is not the shareholder.
Only 6 quarters of reported history. There is no track record here to speak of, and a short series flatters whatever the recent trend happens to be.
No officer history could be reconstructed from public filings, so the team - the thing that matters most - is the thing we know least about.
Base rate: 57.8% of US common stocks underperformed one-month Treasury bills over their lifetimes (Bessembinder, Journal of Financial Economics, 2018). Nothing above changes that starting point.
